name: Denianke Kingdom of Futa Toro
summary: A Fula kingdom on the middle Senegal River, founded by Koli Tenguella and ruled by the Denianke dynasty. It took tribute from many neighbours, then fell to a Muslim revolution in 1776.

location.value: Futa Toro, the middle valley of the Senegal River, immediately south of the Sahara; the north bank is in Mauritania and the south bank in Senegal.
location.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

terrain.value: A narrow river-flood valley, stretching about 250 miles along the Senegal River and never more than about ten miles on either bank.
terrain.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

disasters.value: The summer rains raised the river, which spilled over the banks of the middle valley; this gave a double harvest.
disasters.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

economicBase.value: Mixed farming and cattle herding; the flooded valley made Futa Toro a food-exporting region.
economicBase.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

tradeRoutes.value: At its peak the kingdom controlled the mouth of the Senegal and many trans-Saharan trade routes; from the 17th century French, English and Dutch traders came to buy gold, ivory and slaves.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

governmentType.value: Monarchy under a ruler called the satigi; the Denianke dynasty ruled animist monarchs over an increasingly Muslim population.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

keyRulers.value: Koli Tenguella (died 1537), who founded the dynasty; his brother Labba Tenguella; Satigi Samba Lamu in the early 17th century.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

succession.value: Futa Toro had no clear rules on succession to the satigi, which led to regular power struggles and civil wars.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

stability.value: Unstable in the 18th century: the Trarza Moors, backed by the sultan of Morocco, and the French at Saint-Louis both tried to control the Senegal river trade, causing foreign intervention.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

majorWars.value: Wars against the Mali and Songhai empires; after the Jolof Empire collapsed at the Battle of Danki in 1549, the kingdom took tribute from over a dozen vassal states.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

alliancesRivals.value: Rivals and tributaries included Jolof, Waalo, Cayor, Gajaaga, Diarra and Wagadu; the Trarza Moors and the French at Saint-Louis became rivals in the 1700s.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

religion.value: The kings kept traditional (animist) beliefs while the population became increasingly Muslim; by the 16th century many people and rulers were Muslim, and clerics spread Islam across West Africa.
religion.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro; Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

sharedIdentity.value: The Fulbe of Futa Toro call themselves Haalpulaar'en (Pulaar speakers); French and Wolof usage calls them Toucouleur, from the old state of Takrur.
sharedIdentity.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

neighbours.value: Mali and Songhai empires, Jolof and its successor states, the Moorish emirates to the north, and French trading posts on the river.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

colonisation.value: Futa Toro had limited contact with Portuguese traders in the early 16th century (some slaves supplied); later the French became the main trading partner.
colonisation.source: Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

riseSignals.value: Koli Tenguella's Fula state broke away from Mali's orbit and defeated Jolof-era powers; the Denianke dynasty followed him.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom) (start dates differ: 1464, 1512, 1521 and about 1490 in different sources)

peakPeriod.value: The early 17th century under Satigi Samba Lamu, when the kingdom controlled the Senegal river mouth and trans-Saharan routes.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

declineSignals.value: Succession struggles, civil wars and foreign intervention in the 18th century.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)

outcome.value: Overthrown in 1776 by a Muslim revolution led by Sulayman Bal, which created the Imamate of Futa Toro.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom); Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History: Futa Toro

sources.value: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo; Shillington (ed.), Encyclopedia of African History, 'Futa Toro'. Both read as search excerpts only, 16 Nov 2026.

overallCertainty.value: Much of the early history rests on oral tradition, and sources disagree on the founding date (1464 to 1521) and the kingdom's start.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Empire of Great Fulo (Denanke Kingdom)
